# Backlog archive

Finished items (landed, staging, live and dropped), moved here from [backlog.md](backlog.md) by `pnpm backlog archive`, with their notes; their inbox lines were removed. `pnpm backlog show B-n` and `pnpm backlog list --all` still find them. Don't edit it by hand.

### B-1 · bug · Sign-in can be submitted again while it's loading, and the first load is slow

- status: landed
- prd: quick-fixes
- owner: prd/quick-fixes
- commit: b0325d0

- 2026-11-17 (dev keeper): Likely cause: `sign-in.tsx` disables the button only while `navigation.state === "submitting"`. After the action redirects, the state is `"loading"` while `/app`'s loaders run `waitForFirstSync` (up to 10 s on a device that hasn't synced), and the button is live again. Fix: stay disabled until the navigation is idle. The slowness is separate: the first sync blocks the first screen. Triage it before choosing a shorter cap, rendering local data straight away with a syncing state, or a smaller first bucket.
- 2026-11-17 (plan/quick-fixes): Narrowed to the double submit; the slow first load is now B-22. Quick-fixes slice 1.

### B-12 · plan · Assistant: lightweight chat, with voice, for quick actions and questions about the timeline

- status: landed
- prd: assistant
- owner: prd/assistant
- commit: ed7029d

- 2026-11-17 (dev keeper): Quick actions go through the same local write paths as the forms (offline, synced), as a draft the user confirms. Questions need server-side retrieval and an AI vendor that doesn't retain or train on our data.
- 2026-11-18 (plan/assistant): Draft PRD written on plan/assistant: plans/assistant-prd.md. Interview 2026-11-18: actions first then questions; floating button + sheet; server transcription (vendor open); conversations not saved; drafts confirmed; offline queue (text + audio, drafts wait); opt-in per group (owner consents, members acknowledge); read tools over services; Anthropic TS SDK; model chosen by an eval; create + edit recent; Save as note; 'via assistant' marker; daily caps per user. Questions wait on search's server side.
- 2026-11-19 (plan/encryption): Security review (plans/security-review.md), S-12: the assistant PRD must set AI vendor rules: zero retention in writing, least data per request, no health data in logs, per-group owner opt-in, on-device where possible.
- 2026-11-19 (Robert Bo Davis): User 2026-11-19: the first assistant PRD uses no remote AI: an actions layer (log vital, symptom, dose or pass, note, appointment; what's due; summarize since a date), a quick-entry grammar parsed on the device with a preview, one-tap predictions, simple mode (B-87), templated daily summaries (B-49) and a 'since the last visit' sheet (B-58). Voice is keyboard dictation. On-device models and remote AI calls come later; outside AI goes through the connectors PRD.
- 2026-11-19 (Robert Bo Davis): Quick entry, user 2026-11-19: a pure device parser (lib/quickEntry.ts) → ranked readings; always one best-guess preview with alternatives as chips, nothing saved until Save, Edit opens the full sheet. One line may make several entries (split on commas and 'and'), one preview card each, Save saves all. Order: vitals (keyword + number, bare 120/80; all readings in one entry; user's units, explicit unit wins) → doses (gave/skipped/refused + medication or pass; 'gave all') → symptom with 0-10 → appointment (future time or appt) → note. Time words on any line; past-only kinds refuse future times. Shortcuts: kind prefixes (n: e: s: v: d:), name autocomplete (medications, passes, providers), recent lines as one-tap repeats, a tips line. Placement: simple mode's main input, and always visible on the timeline above the entries (B-98's + menu keeps the per-kind buttons).

- status: landed

- commit: e6fc148

- 2026-11-18 (prd/providers): Found by the providers orchestrator while landing providers slice 1. routing.mjs fails on dev itself (b869738, routing wave 2): 'group settings opens under the group route' fails every run (54/55): after the entry step, c.goto(/app/groups/<id>/settings) renders no main and no window.caretookSync; the only console error is Vite's 'Failed to send error to Vite server: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading send)', which hides the real error. Not reproduced by a standalone script (sign in, open the same seeded note, then settings), so it depends on routing.mjs's earlier state (its proxy browser). One run also failed 'Account's Sign out signs out' and '/app/settings then asks to sign in' (/app/settings/account), possibly load (avg 60-230). Every other check passed on prd/providers.
- 2026-11-18 (prd/providers): Seen again on prd/providers 5dbd62d (providers slice 2 merged): routing.mjs 53/55, failing 'Account's Sign out signs out' and '/app/settings then asks to sign in' at load ~21; the group settings step passed this time. Slice 2's loop saw 55/55.
- 2026-11-18 (Robert Bo Davis): Routing landed in full (ff25ef2) with B-27 still open; prd/routing is closed. In the landing suite routing.mjs passed 80/80 (slice 5 changed the group settings step to open …/settings/members), so this may only be hidden. Slice 3 saw the same blank group settings once, on a long-running server. Next: a quick-fixes slice, or reopen routing, to find the root cause.
- 2026-11-18 (prd/quick-fixes): Seen on prd/quick-fixes ac12b13 (dev ff25ef2 synced in, fresh datastore:reset and dev server): routing.mjs failed 3 runs in a row at load 18-32. Twice 4/5 with 'caretaker: timed out waiting for ol > li' on the timeline right after the settings/members step (Vite 'Failed to send error' again hides the real error); once with dev's own cdp.mjs, 27/29 with 'offline: Quick add → Symptom opens the sheet' and 'TypeError: Illegal invocation'. Every other suite check passed. The pre-sync routing.mjs passed 55/55. Not caused by quick-fixes: its cdp.mjs 401 retry never fired.
- 2026-11-18 (prd/providers): Still failing after routing finished (prd/providers 82eb690, synced with dev 94a0c08): 'group settings opens under the group route' fails at load ~13 (quiet machine), so not contention. Now at /settings/members, same blank page and 'Failed to send error to Vite server'. Rest of routing.mjs 79/80.
- 2026-11-18 (Robert Bo Davis): Moved to quick-fixes slice 7 (routing is closed). Also folds in routing's leftover app-shell.mjs flake (reading window.caretookSync.userId right after a reload).
- 2026-11-18 (slice/quick-fixes/7): Root cause (slice/quick-fixes/7): proxy.mjs didn't handle CONNECT, and Chrome sends WebSockets through a proxy as CONNECT tunnels, so Vite's HMR socket never connected in routing.mjs's proxied caretaker browser ('[vite] failed to connect to websocket'). That page never got 'optimized dependencies changed, reloading', kept its old pre-bundled chunks while newly visited routes imported the new ones, and broke with two copies of React and Yjs ('Yjs was already imported', 'Invalid hook call'): the blank page. Reproduced with the old proxy on a cleared deps cache (79/80, those errors); fixed proxy passes 80/80 through 4 mid-run re-optimizations. Second cause: the offline Quick add step cut the network right after a full load, before React Router had loaded the sheet route modules, so it reloaded the page offline (the Illegal invocation run); the check now waits for those modules. Not fixed: on a server with an empty deps cache, the very first sign-in can still miss Vite's first reload (504 Outdated Optimize Dep on yjs, blank /sign-in; AGENTS.md gotcha). A follow-up could pre-bundle every dep at startup (optimizeDeps.entries over the route modules).
- 2026-11-18 (slice/quick-fixes/7): Two other flakes seen once each on a quiet machine (load 9-12) during slice 7, neither repeated on a rerun and neither through the proxy, so left for another slice: app-shell.mjs 'goes to the last group after a reload' (member@'s /app full load showed an empty body for 20 s with no errors, then reached Grandpa Lou's timeline later, so the next step 'stale remembered group' failed too); routing.mjs 'a reload reopens the edit sheet with the entry's current values' (the reloaded page showed the value from before the server change despite the step's 3 s sleep: the local database's copy not yet saved when the page reloads). Both look like PowerSync's local copy across a full reload. The sign-out failures from earlier runs didn't recur in 8 routing runs; they were probably the same stale-deps breakage.

### B-28 · chore · Limit browser checks machine-wide: a lock so at most two run at once

- status: landed
- prd: quick-fixes
- owner: prd/quick-fixes
- commit: 8eaf3c3

- 2026-11-18 (Robert Bo Davis): Browser checks were 63% of tool time (850 runs, ~10 h) and ~30% failed, mostly timeouts and PowerSync 401s under contention, causing reruns. A wrapper (e.g. pnpm prd browser <check>) takes one of two lock dirs under .loops/.browser/, like the slot leases, waits for a free one, runs the check with the worktree's .env.loop, and releases on exit (including timeouts for signout-wipe and layout-offline). See AGENTS.md, Browser check budget.
- 2026-11-18 (Robert Bo Davis): Planned as quick-fixes slice 4 (plans/quick-fixes-plan.md): pnpm prd browser with two machine-wide leases, --timeout, --suite.
- 2026-11-18 (slice/quick-fixes/4): slice/quick-fixes/4: pnpm prd browser built (2 machine-wide leases, --timeout, --suite, leases in pnpm prd status); hand-off has AGENTS.md wording
- 2026-11-18 (prd/providers): From the providers orchestrator: a check killed by `timeout` (or crashing) leaves its Chrome running on its CDP port; the next run of that check reuses the signed-in browser and fails at 'timed out waiting for input[name=email]'. The wrapper should kill the check's Chrome processes on exit (e.g. by --remote-debugging-port), or cdp.mjs should refuse a port already in use.

- 2026-11-18 (Robert Bo Davis): Found 2026-11-18 running checks against pnpm prd serve --built (a check build, VITE_CHECK_BUILD=1) in a throwaway worktree: providers.mjs failed 'a deleted provider's URL is the 404, with no names' (main empty, body '') and on the retry 'a viewer gets no Add; …/providers/new and …/:id/edit show the list with no form' (path stayed …/providers/new); phase2.mjs failed on '[viewer console.warning] [PowerSync]: Sync aborted'. Both passed against the dev server right after. Could be real production bugs (the 404 and redirect paths) or check timing under a faster server. Fix, then make --built the default for checks (AGENTS.md, Browser check budget).
- 2026-11-18 (Robert Bo Davis): Planned as quick-fixes slice 11 (find the cause of each failure, then make the check build the default).
- 2026-11-18 (slice/quick-fixes/11): Root cause (slice 11): the back/forward cache. On a full load the old /app page is frozen in Chrome's bfcache instead of unloaded; PowerSync's shared workers only drop a page when its tab-close-signal Web Locks are released, so they keep waiting on the frozen page's database connection (often mid-transaction) and the next page's openSync never resolves: blank page, router not initialized, no errors. Evidence: hangs happened exactly when the previous page was bfcached (marker survives Back), 0 hangs with --disable-features=BackForwardCache; a probe that holds a write transaction then full-loads hung 1/5, 2/8, 1/8 before and 0/12, 0/20 after the fix. The dev server never shows it: Vite's HMR websocket keeps pages out of bfcache (0/6 cached on dev, about 1/3 on the build). Fix: lib/sync/pageCache.ts releases PowerSync's page-lifetime locks on pagehide(persisted) and reloads on pageshow(persisted). 'Sync aborted' is the shared sync worker's teardown log for a page that closed, broadcast to the next page: expected, now ignored by the checks.
- 2026-11-18 (slice/quick-fixes/11): slice 11 done on slice/quick-fixes/11 (tip 7da2c38): lib/sync/pageCache.ts fix; checks fixed for the build (per-page x-forwarded-for for Better Auth's production rate limits, tap waits for its target to stop moving, Escape waits for menu focus, picker focus return, 'Sync aborted' ignored); pnpm prd browser now defaults to a check build (--dev opts out). Full suite and dev/build timing deferred to the orchestrator's landing run.

### B-41 · bug · /app stays blank after a full reload (app-shell.mjs last-group steps)

- status: landed
- prd: quick-fixes
- owner: prd/quick-fixes
- commit: 94ce803

- 2026-11-18 (prd/quick-fixes): Seen in quick-fixes waves 3 and 4: after A.goto('/app') reloads, the page has no main and an empty body for 20 s, with no uncaught errors (page.diagnose()). It failed 4 of the last 5 app-shell.mjs runs at load 6–30, at either the 'goes to the last group after a reload' or the 'stale remembered group' step. It isn't a check race: waiting for GroupMenu's rememberGroup write before overwriting caretook:lastGroup didn't help. Probably session or sync startup on reload (requireSession/openSync, the DB lock from the previous page?). Triaged to quick-fixes as a candidate slice 12.
- 2026-11-18 (slice/quick-fixes/11): slice 11 (B-38): providers.mjs's two build failures are this same hang, on the built server: after a full load (C.goto) of …/providers/<deleted id> or …/providers/new, body '' and no main, router state.initialized false, window.caretookSync unset (openSync never resolved), no Web Locks held or pending, no errors, for 20+ s. Reproduced 1 in 8 full loads in a throwaway loop (viewer: provider page, then full load of a deleted provider). So B-38's blank 404 and missing redirect are B-41's startup hang, not the 404 or guard code; slice 11 leaves the fix to slice 12.
- 2026-11-18 (slice/quick-fixes/11): slice 11 found B-38's blank pages are the back/forward cache freezing the previous page with PowerSync's locks held (see B-38's note); fixed in lib/sync/pageCache.ts on slice/quick-fixes/11. On the dev server pages didn't enter bfcache in my tests (Vite's websocket), so B-41 on dev may be a different cause, but worth retesting app-shell.mjs with slice 11 merged.
- 2026-11-18 (slice/quick-fixes/12): Root cause: every full load put the old page in Chrome's back/forward cache (pagehide persisted, then freeze) with its PowerSync connection open. Frozen mid-query, its DB lease was never returned (worker log: 'Closing connection lease that hasn't been returned' 7-13 s later, on eviction), so the next page's powersync.init() waited and /app stayed blank. Fix in lib/sync/client.ts (startup, not sign-out teardown): close the DB on a persisted pagehide, reload on a persisted pageshow. Also fixed app-shell.mjs's stale-group step racing GroupMenu's remember effect. Slice 11: the frozen page's close can log PowerSync's 'error closing database connection' in the shared worker. 41b5bcb, d75e3ba.

The check signed viewer@ in again on the same page that had just signed out (same x-forwarded-for, after a run of session checks), so Better Auth's limiter could answer the first get-session after sign-in with a 429. requireSession treats 429 as 'unknown'; sign-out wiped the cached user, so with no cached user it returns 'signedOut' and redirects to /sign-in with no message (lib/session.ts resolveUser). Harness fixed in slice 7 (fresh page per sign-in). App: a rate-limited session check right after a successful sign-in silently bounces to /sign-in; worth a message or a retry (not changed in slice 7).
- 2026-11-19 (prd/orchestration): orchestration wave 3 landed. app-shell.mjs (now 13 assertions, 8 s) passed on the new suite at low load; every sign-in is on a fresh page, which removes the step 6g repeat sign-in. Probable app cause (unconfirmed, log gone): a 429 on the first get-session after sign-in counts as unknown, and with no cached user requireSession treats it as signed out and redirects to /sign-in silently (apps/web/app/lib/session.ts resolveUser). providers.mjs and admin.mjs weren't rerun here.

### B-130 · bug · A rate-limited session check right after sign-in sends the user back to /sign-in with no message

- status: landed
- prd: quick-fixes
- owner: prd/quick-fixes
- commit: b8d516e

- 2026-11-19 (Robert Bo Davis): From the orchestration PRD (slice 7, investigating B-113's app-shell step 6g). Unconfirmed, the log was gone: a 429 on the first get-session after sign-in counts as unknown, and with no cached user (sign-out wiped it) requireSession treats it as signed out and redirects to /sign-in silently (apps/web/app/lib/session.ts, resolveUser). Likely fix: retry the session check once on 429, or show a 'try again' message instead of a silent redirect.
- 2026-11-19 (Robert Bo Davis): Triage: a contained fix in apps/web/app/lib/session.ts (retry get-session once on 429, or a 'try again' message), so a quick-fixes slice.
- 2026-11-19 (slice/quick-fixes/43): slice 43: 429 on get-session retried once (X-Retry-After, capped 2 s); still 429 with no cached user -> /sign-in?reason=rate-limited with a message. Reproduced on the built server: Better Auth's limiter (on only with NODE_ENV=production) allows 100 get-session per IP per 10 s, then 429 with x-retry-after up to 10, so the 2 s retry usually still 429s and the message shows. Commit 9fc492c.

### B-403 · feature · A cleanup agent every few hours (pnpm prd tidy): finds finished sessions still open, finished worktrees and branches, and other leftovers; removes the safe ones and reports the rest

- status: live
- prd: orchestration-2
- owner: prd/orchestration-2
- commit: 5241714c

- 2026-11-21 (Robert Bo Davis): Asked for by the user 2026-11-21 after a hand sweep by the backlog session. Not covered today: pnpm prd gc only lists merged slice worktrees and stacks stopped over a day, reclaim only disk; neither sees sessions, plan worktrees, branches or stale refs. What the hand sweep checked, as the task list: (1) sessions whose work is done but are still open (an orchestrator or planner whose worktree is gone or whose branch is in dev; idle backlog and stray main-checkout sessions): ask each over cross-session message whether it is done, then report it for closing (slice 2's recorded sessions give the list; closing a tab may need pnpm prd rotate's machinery); (2) worktrees left after the work landed: plan/<topic> worktrees level with dev and with no session, slice worktrees merged into their prd branch; remove with pnpm prd rm; (3) leftovers: local branches with no worktree (report unmerged ones, never delete them unasked), stale remote-tracking refs (git fetch --prune), caretook's dangling Docker volumes, lease and queue tickets whose pid is dead, test databases with no worktree, old .loops/.browser-hangs logs, finished items to archive (pnpm backlog archive) and PRD rows that are done. Rules: never touch a live worktree's build or Vite cache (reclaim --yes would, mid-check), never close a session or delete unmerged work without the user; anything not plainly safe goes to the asks queue (B-391) as one report. Found by hand that day: 4 finished sessions open (one for 5 h), 1 plan worktree, 1 unmerged 2-day-old slice branch, 7 stale remote refs, 6 dangling volumes, 61 items to archive, 4 stale PRD rows. Scheduling: a recurring run every few hours while any PRD runs; fits after slice 2 (sessions) and slice 3 (asks), or as the dispatcher's chore in orchestration-3 (B-392) if the orchestrator finds it too big for this PRD.
- 2026-11-21 (prd/orchestration-2): orchestration-2 slice 7 (wave 5, after slice 6): pnpm prd tidy sorts leftovers into safe (removed with --yes) and ask (one report ask); prompt.sh tidy is the haiku brief, repeated with /loop; the dispatcher's tick in orchestration-3 takes the scheduling over.

### B-408 · feature · Stuck workers handled by the orchestrator: it tracks how long its commands and slice agents have run against their usual time, stops and restarts a stuck one on its own judgement (once), and for a judgement call asks a fresh skeptic agent first and the user through the asks queue only if that doesn't settle it

- status: landed
- prd: worker-watch
- owner: prd/worker-watch
- commit: 1efcd79f

- 2026-11-21 (Robert Bo Davis): Asked for by the user 2026-11-21: unsticking workers is manual work they do often. Triaged to orchestration-3 (hot file scripts/loops/prompt.sh; the dispatcher reopens dead sessions, this covers live-but-stuck ones; asks from B-391). Exists today: browser checks have a 90 s silence limit, a cap and one contention retry (loop.md, Limits); pnpm prd check is timed in .loops/.check-times.log; nothing covers a hung pnpm check, a slice agent that has gone quiet, or a helper subagent. Proposed shape: (1) every long command runs with a budget from its usual time (check-times medians, scaled for load) and a silence limit, and a breach is reported with its last output, not just killed; (2) the orchestrator records each slice agent's start and last sign of progress (commit, file change in its worktree, message) and on no progress messages it, then restarts it once with --continue; (3) a second stall, or a stop that could lose work (uncommitted changes, a migration or landing step under way), is a judgement call: a fresh skeptic agent reads the evidence and decides, and files an ask with a recommendation only when it can't or the step is risky; (4) pnpm prd status shows each running command's and agent's age against its usual time. Open for the PRD: the thresholds, and whether the dispatcher's tick does the watching so an orchestrator that is itself stuck is caught. Could be its own small topic if orchestration-3 passes about six slices (it now has B-392, B-404, B-406, B-407 and this).
- 2026-11-21 (plan/orchestration-3): Moved out of orchestration-3 by its planner (2026-11-21) to keep that PRD at six slices: orchestration-3 is the dispatcher core (B-392, B-426, B-427, B-428, B-439). The grouping and the row order of the four follow-on topics are the planner's; plans/orchestration-3-prd.md, Follow-on topics.
- 2026-11-22 (plan/worker-watch): Planned in plans/worker-watch-prd.md: B-434 is slice 1; B-408 is slices 2 to 6 (check budget, heartbeat and status, the watch, orchestrator response, dispatcher).

The watch should catch 'session waiting on a background command, no check lease, no output, machine quiet'. Direct cause is filed separately under fixes-tooling (check-plan hang).

### B-476 · change · Codex verdict carries over a dev merge that leaves the PR's diff alone

- status: staging
- prd: fixes-tooling
- owner: hotfix/codex-carry
- commit: c660a546

- 2026-11-21 (Robert Bo Davis): User's decision 2026-11-21 (backlog session): planner and backlog commits on dev make PR branches re-wait on Codex after every dev sync. Today a verdict is stale whenever the reviewed sha differs from the head (scripts/loops/codex-review.mjs, reviewedSha !== headSha). New rule: a clean verdict carries forward when all three hold, else stale as now: (1) every commit since the reviewed head is a merge of dev, with no conflict resolution and no new work by the branch; (2) the PR's own diff against dev is unchanged from the reviewed one (same patch id); (3) the incoming dev changes touch none of the files the PR touches. Accepted trade: incoming code in another file that changes the meaning of the PR's code is left to the check gate. To confirm while building: that a carried verdict works with land's GitHub merge pinned to the head, and that review --wait, pr and the orchestrator doc (landing steps 4 and 6) say the same thing. Tests in codex-review.test.mjs and land.test.mjs.

### B-551 · feature · 'bye' for every agent role: a message of just 'bye' runs a handover check; nothing left means the session closes itself, otherwise it asks the user what to do with what's left

- 2026-11-22 (Robert Bo Davis): From the user (backlog session, 2026-11-22): every agent type needs this; details are the agent's. Proposed shape: one shared command (e.g. pnpm prd bye, or a step every role doc points at) that checks the handover state for the session's role: uncommitted or unpushed work, a worktree or branch still out, leases and dev servers held, running background jobs or subagents, open asks it filed, peers waiting on a promised reply, notices to act on, memory to update. Clean: write the hand-off line (what was done, what waits), release leases, run pnpm prd end (or the role's end), and close the session. Not clean: one AskUserQuestion per open thing (finish it, hand it off, drop it), then check again. Each role doc (loop, orchestrator, planner, backlog, hotfix, recovery) names its own extra checks. Fits agent-autonomy-2's session work (recorded sessions B-437, rotate --self B-514); that plan is written, so its orchestrator adds a slice or its planner folds it in.

### B-620 · bug · Timeline day headers repeat a care period day number when the viewer and recipient are in different time zones

- status: landed
- prd: fixes-bug
- owner: prd/fixes-bug
- commit: 62621f1d

- 2026-11-23 (Robert Bo Davis): 2026-11-23, reported by the user with a screenshot: just after midnight Eastern, Today and Yesterday both read 'At home · day 6'. Cause from the code: DayHeader splits days in the viewer's zone (dayKey), but DayPeriod counts periodDay in the recipient's zone from a moment (now for Today, the day's newest row for past days). At 00:34 EST it is still the previous evening in a Los Angeles recipient's zone, so both headers land on one recipient date. The recipient's zone on the user's group was not checked, and this was not reproduced in a test. Proposed fix: in a day header, derive the number from the header's own date, so consecutive headers always differ by one: the period's start date in the recipient's zone to dayKey, plus 1, minimum 1. Keep the period's page and other 'current' lines in the recipient's zone; during the offset hours Today's header can then read one day ahead of the period page, which the user should accept or overrule when reviewing. Which period a header shows (periodAt) should be checked for the same offset. Test with a viewer and recipient in different zones, both sides of midnight (see B-372, a second time zone in tests).
- 2026-11-23 (Robert Bo Davis): 2026-11-23, the user approved the proposed fix: each day header counts from its own date, so consecutive headers always differ by one. Accepted: for a few hours around midnight, Today's header can read one day ahead of the period's page, which stays in the recipient's zone ('nobody will do the math; the display bug will be noticeable'). No further decision needed.

### B-669 · feature · Shared toast system on React Aria: a queue, dismiss and Undo, behind ui/Toast

- status: staging
- prd: fixes-ui
- owner: prd/fixes-ui
- commit: d5356264

- 2026-11-23 (Robert Bo Davis): From the user, 2026-11-23: wants to make heavy use of toasts; agreed no new dependency. First slice of onboarding-2; B-665 (Invite someone toast) builds on it. Use react-aria-components 1.22.1's toast (UNSTABLE_ToastRegion, UNSTABLE_ToastList, UNSTABLE_Toast, UNSTABLE_ToastQueue) only inside ui/, wrapped by the existing ui/Toast, with daisyUI styling. The UNSTABLE_ exports may change on upgrade, so screens must never import them. Needs: a queue so toasts don't overlap, optional action, dismiss, Undo, caller-set timing, reduced motion. Migrate UpdateNotice and AddedMedicationToast. Prove it first on a real phone, above the tab bar and with the keyboard open (see B-664); if it falls short, extend our own component rather than add a library. Usage rules for components.md: toasts for finished actions, Undo, background news and one-time nudges. Not for errors to fix, medically important information, the only path to an action, or the only signal of unsynced changes. Don't sweep the inline Message uses; move one only where a toast is clearly better.

The first save does navigate(appUrls.entry(...), { replace: true }) in useLiveEntry.ts (lines 199 and 227, one-off and repeating), which drops history state unless it's carried over, so carry it. While that mark is present, the back link reads Planner and goes to appUrls.plannerPast when the event is past, else appUrls.planner, decided when the user leaves so a time edited on the page counts. Use the Planner's own rule, isUpcoming/entryTiming in lib/appointments/upcoming.ts: in progress and today's all-day events count as Upcoming. An abandoned unsaved draft returns to the tab it was opened from. Deleting that event (EntryPageHeader.tsx:146, useLiveEntry.ts:342) should also return to the Planner rather than the Timeline. Entries opened any other way keep the Timeline link. Add browser tests for a past event, a future event, an in-progress event and a time changed before leaving.
- 2026-11-23 (Robert Bo Davis): User decision, 2026-11-23: existing events opened from the Planner should also return to the Planner, specifically to where the event was opened. This extends the item. Two rules: a NEW event added from the Planner goes to Past or Upcoming by its time when leaving. An EXISTING event opened from a Planner row goes back to the tab it was opened from, even if its time was edited so it now belongs on the other tab, with that tab's URL filters kept and its scroll position restored where the router allows. Pass the opener's full URL (path and search) in the row links' history state on Upcoming and Past, and label the back link Planner. Deleting an existing event opened this way also returns to that opener. A reload should keep the return path if history state survives; a direct link or bookmark has no opener and keeps the Timeline link. Add browser tests for opening from Upcoming and from Past with a filter set, including Back after editing the time.

### B-696 · bug · check-plan can hang forever or wrongly report no changes when called by hand, which stalled two orchestrators for hours

- status: landed
- prd: fixes-tooling
- owner: prd/fixes-tooling
- commit: 8c921e3e

- 2026-11-23 (Robert Bo Davis): 2026-11-23 incident: dose-accuracy (about 9 h) and fixes-bug (about 4 h) ran 'node scripts/loops/check-plan.mjs --base dev' in a chained background command ahead of pnpm prd check --quick. The CLI reads stdin to EOF before looking at flags (check-plan.mjs:150); stdin never closed, so the check never started, no lease was taken, and the session waited for an exit notice. Also verified: --propose takes changed files only from stdin, so empty stdin prints 'none / no changes' even on a branch with changes. land and pr are safe (propose_tier in lib.sh pipes the diff). Fix: (1) validate args before reading stdin: require --mode or --propose, refuse unknown flags; a TTY check alone would not catch this, because a background stdin need not be a TTY. (2) With --propose and --base/--head, compute the diff itself rather than trusting empty stdin. (3) Add one pnpm prd command that prints the proposed tier, and name it in the orchestrator prompt and handbook, which today say to use the proposed tier with no command. (4) Orchestrator rule: don't chain a lookup ahead of a long check; confirm the check holds a lease (pnpm prd status) before reporting it as running. Touches scripts/loops/prd.sh and prompt.sh, hot for test-gates-2 and worker-watch.

### B-805 · question · Can the PWA sync in the background after offline work, or does the user have to open it to sync?

- status: landed
- prd: sync-safety-2
- owner:
- commit: c79b3ee4

- 2026-11-24 (Robert Bo Davis): Likely answer: iOS installed PWAs have no Background Sync (WebKit), so pending uploads wait until the app is opened. Chrome/Android has the Background Sync API, but PowerSync's upload queue runs in the page, so today it waits too. Options: sync on open/focus (now), a service-worker sync on Android only, or native (Capacitor) background tasks later.
- 2026-11-25 (plan/sync-safety-2): Answered in plans/sync-safety-2 (2026-11-25): no background upload; queued changes upload while the app is open, on open and on reconnect. iOS has no Background Sync and PowerSync's queue runs in the page; native background tasks wait for Capacitor. Written into docs/domain/sync.md; done at the plan's landing.

### B-830 · bug · Staging's seeded invite link shows 'Couldn't load this link': the Seed and Reset staging Actions seal it without INVITE_LINK_KEY

- status: landed
- prd: fixes-bug
- owner: prd/fixes-bug
- commit: 9dd61dda

- 2026-11-25 (Robert Bo Davis): User report 2026-11-25 with screenshot: Members page, Invite links, the seeded Viewer link (made by Dev Member) shows 'Couldn't load this link. Reload the page to try again.', Copy and Share disabled. Cause: seed-staging.yml (and reset-staging.yml's seed step) pass only APP_ENV, DATABASE_URL and SEED_USER_PASSWORD, so seeds/invites.ts sealLinkToken uses linkToken.ts's DEV_KEY; the staging server opens with the real INVITE_LINK_KEY, so careGroupInviteService.copyLink returns linkKeyMissing. Fix: pass INVITE_LINK_KEY from the staging environment's secrets to both Actions' seed step, then reseed or reset staging. Consider making the seed refuse to seal with the dev key when APP_ENV is staging, so a missing key fails loudly. Links made by hand on staging are not affected (inferred from code, not checked).

A fresh session's background recheck got 'signed out' (~10 ms locally, ~60 ms more to close the device) before the timeline loader's two DB rounds (the tag read from tags slice 6, a5b63301, is the first, ~37 ms) committed the ?kind=symptom address, so location.assign used the old URL (redirectTo lost kind=symptom) or unloaded the page before the filtered list showed. Fix: session.ts recheck uses the navigation's target while the address hasn't moved (unit-tested); the spec holds get-session until the filtered timeline shows. Follow-up idea: read tags in the loader's second round unless ?tag= is set.

- 2026-11-26 (slice/fixes-tooling/79): Cause (fixes-tooling slice 79): after Back, the timeline's ~38 watches run one at a time, and each batched frame of results (B-633) rendered the 3-page timeline between them, holding up the queries behind it. At a 4x CPU throttle it reproduces CI's failure exactly (settle timeout, care_period/care_group_member owed). Fix: watchLiveQuery holds the frame, up to 500 ms, while any watch's first result is owed, so a remount renders once. Post-Back settle 0.74-0.87 -> 0.52 s locally, >5 s -> 1.9 s at 4x, 3.4 s at 6x. 10/10 at load 25-133. Quarantine line removed. Follow-up idea: 11 of the 38 watches are duplicates (same SQL and params); sharing them would save about 30% more.

Leads to check first: a cold dev load (Vite unbundled modules, the PowerSync worker and WASM) taking over 10 s to connect; dev server restarts or HMR reloads; the local PowerSync container closing streams or its token refresh (auth.ts 5-minute token) dropping connected for longer than the retry. Idle probes: token refresh 25 ms, PowerSync restart 5 s, serve restart 2 s, HMR none. Fix: 10 s grace only when the browser is offline; 30 s while online (90 s on dev).
